failure_modes.description: Local optimization demonstrably does NOT lead to global optimization in traffic networks
failure_modes.evidence: Decades of traffic engineering research shows that selfish local optimization creates Braess paradox effects and system-wide degradation

failure_modes.description: Queue length as primary performance metric ignores critical factors like pedestrian safety, emergency vehicle access, and emissions
failure_modes.evidence: Real-world traffic systems must balance multiple objectives, not just vehicle queue length

failure_modes.description: The assumption of independent intersection operation fails at network scale
failure_modes.evidence: Traffic networks are inherently interconnected; changes at one intersection propagate through the system

failure_modes.description: The proposed mechanism would immediately fail in any realistic network with moderate traffic
failure_modes.evidence: Basic traffic engineering principles show that uncoordinated signal timing creates stop-and-wave propagation that increases overall delay

failure_modes.description: Minimizing local waiting time conflicts with other critical system objectives
failure_modes.evidence: Emergency vehicle response, transit priority, and pedestrian safety would be compromised by pure queue-length optimization

failure_modes.description: Numerous existing adaptive signal systems have already demonstrated the limitations of local-only optimization
failure_modes.evidence: SCATS, SCOOT, and other major traffic control systems all incorporate network-level coordination
